nodes.label: changeConfig
nodes.responsibility: Coordinates config change: locks, mutates raw config, calls decode/run, and rollbacks on error.

nodes.label: config store
nodes.responsibility: Holds current raw configuration (rawCfg, rawCfgJSON, rawCfgIndex).

nodes.label: unsyncedDecodeAndRun
nodes.responsibility: Decodes new config into a Config and runs it, returns error if run fails, after success stops old context.

nodes.label: run
nodes.responsibility: Provisions new context and starts applications.

nodes.label: app startup
nodes.responsibility: Starts each application from new config; on failure stops already started apps and returns error.

nodes.label: unsyncedStop
nodes.responsibility: Emits stopping, stops all applications, and cancels the old context.

nodes.label: old context
nodes.responsibility: Represents the currently running configuration that continues until new config is running.

edges.verb: indexes new config objects before loading
reports success or failure to run
restores prior raw config on error

question_overlay.summary: Caddy replaces configuration by first mutating the current raw config into a new one, then decoding and running it (provisioning and starting apps) while the old config continues running. Only after the new apps start successfully does it stop the old context. Failures during indexing, provisioning, or app startup cause a rollback that restores the previous raw config, leaving the old config intact.
unknowns: What happens if the admin server replacement during provisioning fails?
Observations do not specify whether restoring raw config on error is atomic or how it handles concurrent config change requests.
